summary: Refero's typography guide for product and marketing UI. It starts from context questions, offers a safe SaaS preset (Inter, 16px, 1.55 line height, 1.2 scale, 65ch), and then covers type scale ratios with a ready Minor Third scale, the one-font rule and pairing strategies, a text color system by opacity, weights, line height, vertical rhythm derived from line height, letter spacing by size and case, measure, punctuation and text-polish details, fluid and stepped responsive type, and font loading. It lists AI-slop red flags with countable limits (8 sizes, 4 colors, 4 weights) and closes with a pre-ship checklist and a complete token set. For a design system it supplies concrete defaults and limits for nearly every typography decision.
key_ideas: Decide context first: work tools need neutrality; when in doubt go denser, simpler and more neutral
A safe SaaS preset already gives good typography; everything else is refinement
Pick one scale ratio and stick to it; Minor Third 1.2 is the default
One family with several weights is the professional default; a second font needs a real reason
Text color comes from a few opacity levels, never pure black, and body never under 60% opacity
Larger text can be lighter; smaller text needs more weight; body is always 400
Line height: body 1.5-1.7, headlines 1.0-1.2, UI 1.2-1.4; longer lines need more
Derive vertical spacing from line height: half the line height is the minimum step
Spacing matters more than font size
Tracking: positive for small text, labels and all caps; negative for large headings; always in em
Keep body measure at 50-75 characters, about 65ch
Polish details: real ellipsis, curly quotes, non-breaking spaces, tabular numbers, balanced headings
Load at most 2 families and 3 weights with font-display: swap; system stack is fine

rules.rule: Before choosing fonts, answer: work tool or marketing, long reading or scanning, B2B, B2C or dev tool; in work products choose neutrality over personality.
rules.why: Context changes line height, density, character and weight choices.

rules.rule: Start from the safe SaaS preset: Inter with system-ui fallback, 16px base, 1.55 line height, 1.2 scale, weights 400/500/600, 65ch max width.
rules.why: If you use this preset as-is, your typography is already good.

rules.rule: Pick one type scale ratio and stick to it; use Minor Third 1.200 by default, 1.067-1.125 for dense UI, 1.250-1.333 for marketing and expressive layouts, and 1.618 only for landing page heroes.
rules.why: A consistent scale creates visual rhythm.

rules.rule: Use no more than 6-8 font sizes in production.
rules.why: More = chaos; 10+ sizes is an AI-slop red flag.

rules.rule: Use one font family with multiple weights; add a second only for marketing pages, content-heavy products or real art direction, and almost never a third.
rules.why: Two fonts adds complexity that must be justified.

rules.rule: When pairing, contrast structure (serif with sans, not two serifs) and match x-heights.
rules.why: Pairing rules.

rules.rule: Never use pure black for text; use #0B0B0B to #111.
rules.why: Listed under Rules That Actually Work: never pure black, use #0B0B0B–#111.

rules.rule: Keep 3-4 text color levels (primary 100%, secondary 65%, tertiary 45%, disabled 30%) and never set readable body text below 60% opacity.
rules.why: Fewer shades with stable usage; lighter text destroys readability.

rules.rule: Do not lighten text for an airy feel; if it fails the squint test it is too light.
rules.why: Almost always destroys readability.

rules.rule: In dark mode use #F5F5F5 for primary text, rgba(255,255,255,0.7) for secondary and rgba(255,255,255,0.5) for tertiary.
rules.why: Dark Mode Inversion tokens.

rules.rule: Set body text at 400 and never bold whole paragraphs; use 500 for UI labels, 600 for buttons and subheadings, 400-700 for headlines depending on the font (serifs often look better at 400); use 300 only for large display text.
rules.why: Weight creates hierarchy; bold everywhere flattens it.

rules.rule: Use 400 minimum and preferably 500 for small text like 12px captions; do not use light 300 below 16px.
rules.why: Smaller size needs heavier weight; light becomes illegible.

rules.rule: Set line height to 1.5-1.7 for body, 1.4-1.5 for short paragraphs, 1.0-1.2 for headlines, 0.9-1.1 for large display, 1.2-1.4 for UI text and 1 for buttons.
rules.why: Line height affects readability most.

rules.rule: Give 80+ character lines 1.6-1.7 leading, 40-character lines about 1.4, and sans-serif about 0.1 more than serif.
rules.why: Longer lines need more leading.

rules.rule: Derive the minimum vertical spacing step from line height × 0.5 (e.g. 16px/1.5 gives 24px lines, 12px step, 12/24/48 scale).
rules.why: Bad spacing between text blocks exposes AI-slop.

rules.rule: Fix spacing before tweaking fonts.
rules.why: Same fonts with different spacing look like different products.

rules.rule: Add letter spacing of 0.06em-0.10em to all-caps text, 0.01em-0.02em to 11-13px small text, and 0.01em-0.03em to UI labels and buttons.
rules.why: Without tracking caps look cramped and small text is harder to read.

rules.rule: Tighten large headings (32px+) to 0 to -0.02em and display text (48px+) to -0.02em to -0.03em, only for non-light headlines where pairs like AV, WA, To do not collide.
rules.why: Large headlines feel loose without tightening.

rules.rule: Always specify letter spacing in em, never px.
rules.why: Em scales with font size.

rules.rule: Keep body text measure at 50-75 characters (about 65ch, minimum 45, maximum 85) and cap compact UI descriptions near 45ch.
rules.why: Optimal reading width prevents eye fatigue.

rules.rule: Use the ellipsis character instead of three dots, curly quotes, and non-breaking spaces between numbers and units and in keyboard shortcuts; end loading labels with an ellipsis.
rules.why: Polish details AI models often miss.

rules.rule: Use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums for tables, prices, counters and stats.
rules.why: Proportional figures make digits different widths.

rules.rule: Apply text-wrap: balance to short headings, captions, pull quotes and card titles and text-wrap: pretty to lead and prose, but not to nav, buttons, tables, badges, code, form controls or dense labels.
rules.why: Prevents one-word last lines that look accidental.

rules.rule: Make text containers handle long content with truncation, line clamp or word breaking, and give flex children min-width: 0 so text can truncate.
rules.why: Flex children otherwise will not truncate.

rules.rule: Scale type with viewport non-linearly using clamp() or breakpoints: base 16px to 16-18px, H1 32-36px to 48-64px, keeping letter spacing the same.
rules.why: Font size should respond to viewport, but not linearly.

rules.rule: Load at most 2 font families and 3 weights per family, prefer variable fonts, and always use font-display: swap.
rules.why: Beautiful typography on a slow page is bad typography.

rules.rule: Do not center paragraphs except short marketing copy, and do not use a decorative display font without brand intent.
rules.why: Listed as instant red flags that reveal AI-generated or amateur design.

rules.rule: Check that an interface has at most 8 font sizes, 4 text colors and 4 font weights.
rules.why: More is likely AI-slop or needs editing.

rules.rule: Test hierarchy with a squint test (3 clear levels), a 5-second test and a scan test.
rules.why: Clear hierarchy guides the eye.

rules.rule: Meet WCAG AA text contrast: 4.5:1 for body and 3:1 for large text; test layouts at 320px, 768px and 1440px.
rules.why: Pre-ship checklist.

rules.rule: Keep small text at 11px minimum, with positive tracking.
rules.why: Pre-ship checklist item.

rules.rule: Keep disabled text rare; if a screen has lots of disabled text, redesign it.
rules.why: Rules That Actually Work: Disabled is rare.

rules.rule: After applying text-wrap, inspect the real breakpoints; if wrapping is still awkward, adjust copy, max-width, font-size or line-height instead of trusting CSS alone.
rules.why: A single word on the last line of a hero title usually looks accidental.

rules.rule: Build hierarchy in this order of impact: size, weight, color, case (caps for labels), spacing, then italic (rarely); do not make everything bold or use italic everywhere.
rules.why: Everything bold means nothing is bold; italic everywhere is meaningless emphasis.
rules.evidence: Hierarchy Checklist: Visual Weight Stack; Anti-patterns

rules.rule: Use the system font stack (system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', sans-serif) when a custom font is not needed.
rules.why: It loads instantly, looks native and is perfectly professional.

caveats: Opinionated guide from Refero's skill; claims such as 'typography is 90% of web design' are rhetoric, not measurements.
The weights checklist is inconsistent: the quick test allows 4 weights while elsewhere 400/500/600 is 'enough' and ≤3 weights are loaded. [inferred]
The safe preset uses 1.55 line height and rgba(0,0,0,0.7)/0.5 text colors, while the text color system section uses 0.65/0.45; the two sets differ. [inferred]
The scale's pixel values (19, 23, 33, 57) are rounded from the 1.2 ratio. [inferred]
text-wrap: balance and pretty depend on modern browser support; the source says they degrade gracefully.
